narratives.Overview:
1. Explainer. A new exported `explainTextStrictAxes(item)` in `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` builds the same joined, lowercased, slash-split text that `inferTextStrictAxes` matches today, with an index map from each character back to its field and original index, and runs the same regexes over all matches. Per axis it returns up to 3 matches and a count of the rest. Each match gives the field holding its start, `crossField: true` when it ends in another field, and an excerpt: the matched words plus up to four words either side, sliced from the original field text through the map. `inferTextStrictAxes` takes its axis list from the explainer, so decision and explanation cannot drift.
2. Declared axes. When a declaration decides the axes, the report names the field that held the winning token and its value, using the existing precedence of the eight fields.
3. Fence. Every printed excerpt is cut to 80 characters first and then passed through `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText`.
4. Refusal detail. For an unsuitable `evidence.kind`, the `scope:complete` detail adds one continuation line per reported match (`<axis> from <field>: <excerpt>`, then `(+N more)`), or the declared field from item 2. When more than one strict axis is required, it says that no single evidence kind satisfies the clause.
5. Refusal remedy. When a blocker is an axis mismatch, the gate's closing text for that item replaces "Write evidence/disposition on the plan item at the reported path" with: record evidence of the required kind, or an operator runs `formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand` with `not_applicable`, the plan id when present and the item id. It states that the grant disposes of the whole criterion and replaces its evidence, that the grant is bound to the clause text (`clause.N` ids) or the item title only, and that #7127 tracks a correction that keeps test evidence. An item without an id is reported as not targetable by a grant. The refusal does not suggest rewording the clause or adding a declaration. `formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand` and its template-name constant move into `scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`; `policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts` re-exports them.
6. Advisories. At `scope:promote`, `scope:activate` and `xbrief:preflight` each row keeps its current text, and its reported matches print on indented continuation lines under it. At promote and activate the last line also says that a `merge` declaration means no strict axis, so test, review or merge evidence then passes. At `xbrief:preflight` the last line names the item 5 grant command and still does not suggest a declaration.
7. The classifier's results do not change, and existing axis expectations stay as they are.
8. One PR: `acceptance-evidence.ts` and its tests, the re-export in `policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts`, the tests that assert advisory output (`packages/core/src/scope/main.test.ts`, runtime preflight tests), one sentence in `content/commands.md` that shows the `not_applicable` grant, and one `changelog.d/` fragment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Given the #7099 criterion as an item title, when `explainTextStrictAxes` runs, then it returns `deploy` with field `title`, `crossField: false` and an excerpt that contains "deployment" in its original case.
- [ ] Given every string in the existing axis tests, plus title `observed` with id `behavior` and title `user` with id `acceptance`, then the explainer's axis set equals `inferRequiredStrictAxes` with no declaration, the two cross-field cases report `crossField: true`, and no existing axis expectation changes.
- [ ] Given an item with `x-directive/requires: merge` and `x-directive/acceptanceAxis: deploy` and `kind: test` evidence, then the refusal names `x-directive/acceptanceAxis=deploy` as the deciding field.
- [ ] Given an item with an id, a deploy-axis title and `kind: test` evidence, when `scope:complete` refuses, then the refusal shows the fenced excerpt, prints the `not_applicable` grant command with that item id, says the grant replaces the evidence for the whole criterion and is bound to the clause text or title only, names #7127, and does not tell the author to write a disposition onto that item.
- [ ] Given the same item without an id, then the refusal says that no grant can target it.
- [ ] Given "Smoke must pass after deployment" with `kind: smoke` evidence, then the refusal says that no single evidence kind satisfies the clause.
- [ ] Given a matched field that contains a backtick, `»` and a newline near the match, then every output prints the excerpt inside one fence from `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText`, with at most 80 characters before fencing.
- [ ] Given an item with five matches for one axis, then three excerpts print, followed by `(+2 more)`.
- [ ] Given the promote, activate and preflight advisories, then each existing row text is unchanged and its matches follow on continuation lines; the promote and activate last line says what a `merge` declaration admits; the preflight last line names the grant command and no declaration.

## In plain English
`scope:complete` will not accept test evidence for a criterion that it thinks needs a deployment. It decides that by looking for the words deploy, deploys, deployed or deployment in the criterion text. In the consumer repo a criterion described how an event bridge handles deployment-status events ("When a deployment moves failed then rolled_back ..."). Nothing in it is deployed, and a unit test proves it, but the word "deployment" made the gate demand deploy evidence, so the story could not complete without an operator grant. The error named the axis but not the word that caused it, or what to do.

The recommended fix keeps the word rule as it is, because a sentence such as "the deployment succeeds on staging" is a real deploy claim with the same shape as the issue's example. Instead, every place that reports a strict axis also shows the text that set it and where it was found: the activation advisory (so an author can declare the clause's real requirement before activation, when the declaration is reviewed), and the `scope:complete` refusal, which also names the operator grant that clears the clause after activation. No change to which clauses need which evidence.

## Pains
- P1 — A criterion that only describes how code handles deployment data blocks `scope:complete` on `kind: test` evidence, because the word "deployment" sets the deploy axis; the author finds out at completion, when the only paths left are an operator grant or rewording the clause, which edits the gate's input (#7099, #3156).
- P2 — The refusal and the activation advisory name the axis but not the text that set it, or the ways to clear it, so the author cannot see why the axis applied or what to do (#7099, suggested fix 3).

## Out of scope (named, not pains)
- The smoke, UAT and observed-behaviour axes, except that they share the reporting change.
- Inference from code spans and fences (settled by the #6301 arc: keep matching).
- The `x-directive/requires` declaration rules and the #6591 warning, beyond naming them in messages.
- The operator grant (`acceptance-disposition`, #6318), beyond naming it.

## Evidence
- The issue's premise "the only agent-side workaround is to reword" is not quite right. Two other paths exist: an `x-directive/requires` declaration on the item (`merge`, or the one axis it needs), and an operator `acceptance-disposition` grant with `--disposition not_applicable`. But a declaration added after activation is warned by `verify:scope-provenance` (#6591), and that warning's remedy says to remove the added declaration or record the evidence (`refusal-declarations/table.ts`, row `declaration-hides-axis`). So after activation the sanctioned path is the operator grant; before activation a declaration is a reviewed precommitment.
- Parent probe (a scratch `tsx` script outside the repo, importing `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`; `packages/core/src/scope/` is byte-identical between the primary checkout used for the run and the dispatch SHA) of `inferRequiredStrictAxes({ title })`:
  - the issue's criterion: `["deploy"]`; with the "deployment moves" sentence removed (only `deploy.done` left): `[]`.
  - `deploy` for "after deployment", "Works after deployment.", "The service answers after deployment to staging.", "deploys to prod after merge", "the deployment succeeds on staging", "The deployment status page shows rolled_back", "deployment records are stored with their status", "Deployment events are forwarded to the websocket".
  - `[]` for "the deployments table lists failed runs" and "a redeployment is triggered" (`deploy(?:ment|ed|s)?` matches neither "deployments" nor "redeployment").
  - `["smoke","deploy"]` for "Smoke must pass after deployment".
  - With the issue's criterion: `x-directive/requires: merge` gives `[]`; `test` and `review` are not declaration tokens and leave `["deploy"]`; `deploy` gives `["deploy"]`.
- The same probe through `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` with `kind: test` evidence reproduces the issue's error text exactly (`evidence.kind=test is not suitable for required axis/axes [deploy]; merge/review alone cannot satisfy ...`); the item with `x-directive/requires: merge` passes. `formatStrictAxisAdvisory(..., "scope:activate")` prints `a: deploy` with no text, and `b: deploy (declared)`.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`: 383-404 `inferRequiredStrictAxes` (declaration wins; merge-only gives `[]`); 411-418 `inferHiddenStrictAxes`; 421-455 `inferTextStrictAxes` (fields: title, id, narrative Acceptance / Description / Test); 464-472 `PROSE_LEFT`, `PROSE_RIGHT`, `proseWord`, `PROSE_DEPLOY`; 475-489 slash alternations; 546-560 `listStrictAxisRequirements`; 575-622 `formatStrictAxisAdvisory`, `strictAxisAdvisoryLines`; 636-653 `isEvidenceKindSuitable`; 1913-1930 the unsuitable-kind detail; 2407-2449 `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` message.
- `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.test.ts` 267-269: "deploys to prod after merge", "after deployment", "Works after deployment." expect `["deploy"]`.
- `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/declaration-hides-axis.ts` 1-21 (#6591, warn only); `packages/core/src/refusal-declarations/table.ts` 96-101.
- `packages/core/src/policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts` 54 (`deferred`, `not_applicable`, `waived`); `content/commands.md` 155 and 162.
- History: #6270 / #6289 (prose-only boundaries, `deploy.done` excluded); #6301 (keep matching inside code; name-only relief moved to #6591); #6272 / #6369 (activation advisory).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- D1. One matcher, with sources. `inferTextStrictAxes` becomes a thin wrapper over a new exported `explainTextStrictAxes(item)` that returns, per axis, the field it matched in (`title`, `id`, or `narrative.<key>`) and a short excerpt: the matched word with up to four words either side, cut at 80 characters, as written (case kept). Same regexes, same field order, one pass, so the explanation and the decision cannot drift.
- D2. `scope:complete` detail. When `evidence.kind` is unsuitable and the axes come from text, the detail adds one `<axis> from <field>: «<excerpt>»` per axis, fenced with `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText`. When they come from a declaration, it says `declared by x-directive/requires=<value>`.
- D3. `scope:complete` remedy line, printed once when any blocker is an axis mismatch: record evidence of that kind; or, if the clause does not need that event, an operator records `deft authz:grant -- --template acceptance-disposition --plan-ref <scopeId> --story-ids <itemIds> --disposition not_applicable --reason <text> --confirm`. It does not suggest rewording the clause or adding a declaration after activation.
- D4. Advisory. Each row printed at `scope:promote`, `scope:activate` and `xbrief:preflight` adds the same `from <field>: «<excerpt>»`. At promote and activate the existing last line already names the declaration; it stays.
- D5. The classifier does not change: same words, same fields, same results for every existing test.
- D6. Tests: `explainTextStrictAxes` on the issue's criterion (deploy, the field, an excerpt containing "deployment"); the gate detail and the remedy line; an advisory row with the excerpt; an excerpt with backticks and `»` stays inside the fence; the existing axis tests stay unchanged.
- D7. One PR: `acceptance-evidence.ts`, its tests, and one `changelog.d/` fragment.

Questions for the critics:
1. Is keeping the classifier (D5) right? Or is there a rule that clears the issue's criterion while "after deployment", "the service answers after deployment to staging" and "the deployment succeeds on staging" still need deploy evidence, and no real deploy claim passes on test evidence?
2. Does D1-D4 relieve P1, given that after activation the only sanctioned path is still an operator grant? If not, what is the smallest change that does (for example a `test` declaration token, which today does not exist and would not admit merge evidence the way `merge` does)?
3. Is D3 honest about #6591? Should the refusal mention the declaration at all?
4. Is the excerpt (D1, D2) safe and useful: length bound, case, fencing of untrusted text, and more than one match per axis?
5. Does this fit one PR?

## In plain English

The gate mistakes deployment data for a requirement to deploy something. The proposed change explains that mistake but deliberately preserves it. That is useful diagnostic work, but it does not make the consumer repo’s test evidence sufficient.

I support preserving classification in this PR, with corrections below. D3 must disclose that its grant replaces acceptance evidence with a disposition for the whole criterion. D1 also needs an explicit way to preserve matches spanning fields. I would not bind D1–D7 unchanged or describe them as resolving P1.

## Answers to questions 1–5

1. **Keep D5 for this diagnostic slice.** The inspected matcher cannot establish whether a deployment noun describes data or an actual event. I have no replacement text rule with the requested no-false-negative guarantee. Existing classification already misses “redeployment”; preserving it is compatibility, not proof of semantic correctness.
2. **D1–D4 improve discovery and recovery instructions, but leave P1’s completion blockage.** A `test` declaration could avoid the extra merge permission granted by `merge`, but alone would not solve post-activation authority. Keep P1 explicit as residual rather than add a new declaration mechanism to this PR.
3. **D3 is consistent with avoiding post-activation declaration edits, but must distinguish policy from enforcement.** #6591 warns; it does not refuse completion. Mention an existing declaration when explaining a decision, but do not recommend adding one as completion-time recovery.
4. **Bounded, fenced excerpts are useful with qualifications.** Preserve the actual match, label a single example as a trigger rather than an exhaustive explanation, handle cross-field matches, and fence excerpts in advisories too. The existing fence is an untrusted-content marker, not comprehensive terminal or Markdown sanitization.
5. **One PR is reasonable for diagnostics and regression coverage.** Keep semantic reclassification and new authority mechanisms outside it. Treat D7’s file list as an estimate, not a restriction that prevents necessary tests.

## Findings

### 1. blocks-the-design — D3 offers a whole-criterion disposition as though it clears only the false axis

**Evidence:** At the dispatch pin, `applyGrantedDispositions` calls `stampNamespacedDisposition`. That calls `clearAcceptanceStampFields`, deleting existing evidence. `evaluateAcceptanceEvidenceGate` accepts a valid disposition without testing evidence suitability. The grant template supports `not_applicable`, but has no axis-specific exemption.

**Failure mode:** An operator follows “if the clause does not need that event” and marks the whole event-handling requirement not applicable. The requirement remains applicable and tested; only the inferred deployment obligation was wrong. The resulting acceptance record loses that distinction and replaces its test evidence.

**Disposition consequence:** Rewrite D3 to state that the command authorizes a disposition of the entire criterion and replaces its evidence record. Do not present it as accepting the existing test or correcting the classifier. Retain P1 as unresolved unless a separately scoped mechanism preserves test-backed acceptance while correcting the requirement.

### 2. blocks-the-design — A single-field explanation cannot represent every existing match

**Evidence:** `inferTextStrictAxes` joins title, id and narrative fields with newlines before matching. `PROSE_USER_ACCEPTANCE` uses `user\s+acceptance`; observed-behavior matching also permits whitespace. A read-only Node probe confirmed matches across `"user\nacceptance"` and `"observed\nbehavior"`.

**Failure mode:** An item with title `user` and id `acceptance` currently requires UAT, even though neither field independently contains the matching phrase. Searching each field separately would change classification; retaining the joined search but attributing the complete match to one field would misdescribe the evidence.

**Disposition consequence:** D1 must retain the joined matching surface and map match spans back to their contributing fields, or explicitly represent a cross-field trigger. Add regression cases for both examples. Preserve slash-alternation matching and map excerpts back to original text rather than transformed offsets.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Declaration explanations must identify the winning field

**Evidence:** `readExplicitAcceptanceRequirementFields` reads eight fields. `inferRequiredStrictAxes` selects the first valid strict declaration and gives it precedence over a merge declaration.

**Failure mode:** With `x-directive/requires=merge` and `x-directive/acceptanceAxis=deploy`, deploy is required. D2’s prescribed `declared by x-directive/requires=<value>` could blame `merge`, or invent a value in a field that was absent.

**Disposition consequence:** Explain the actual winning declaration field and normalized value using the existing precedence. Add conflicting-field and alias fixtures. This refines diagnostics without changing authority.

### 4. sharpens-framing — D3’s evidence remedy is impossible for some supported inputs

**Evidence:** `isEvidenceKindSuitable` requires every inferred axis to equal one evidence kind. Its documentation explicitly identifies the multi-axis limitation. `"Smoke must pass after deployment"` infers both smoke and deploy.

**Failure mode:** “Record evidence of that kind” suggests an available repair, but neither smoke nor deploy evidence can satisfy that criterion through this gate.

**Disposition consequence:** Qualify the remedy for multi-axis blockers: no single evidence kind satisfies them under the current representation. Do not imply an axis-specific grant exists. This is necessary honesty for a shared diagnostic surface, not a request to redesign multi-axis acceptance here.

### 5. sharpens-framing — P2 relief must not be counted as P1 resolution

**Evidence:** Existing mechanisms already include pre-activation advisories, declaration precedence, the warning-only provenance comparison, and operator disposition grants. D5 preserves classification and evidence suitability.

**Failure mode:** Closing the reported false-positive problem after this PR leaves the same test-backed criterion blocked; the user merely receives a better explanation.

**Disposition consequence:** Describe the deliverable as trigger visibility and recovery guidance. Explicitly retain the unwanted operator intervention as residual pain.

## Alternatives considered

The strongest case for a `test` declaration is that it expresses the intended proof without also admitting merge evidence. I would reconsider it with a defined post-activation authorization rule and tests showing that it cannot silently erase a real deployment requirement. Adding the token alone does not establish either property.

## Verification and limits

## What happened

`scope:complete` refused a story because one criterion contains the word "deployment". It treats the criterion as needing a `deploy` evidence axis, although the criterion describes code behaviour that a unit test proves.

The criterion (consumer repo, item 2):

> When a deployment moves failed then rolled_back with both callbacks delayed until after the second write, the bridge sends exactly one deploy.done frame with status failed and one with status rolled_back (in either order, since bus callbacks run concurrently), and the notification subscriber announces each status once.

The criterion is about how an event bridge handles deployment-status events. Nothing in it is deployed. `api/internal/websocket/devops-bridge_test.go` covers it, at the merge commit of the product PR.

## Output (directive 0.131.0)

```
Error: Acceptance evidence required for scope:complete (#3240 / #3305). 1 criterion/criteria missing suitable evidence or disposition:
  - plan.items[1] «untrusted:When a deployment moves failed then rolled_back …»: evidence.kind=test is not suitable for required axis/axes [deploy]; merge/review alone cannot satisfy smoke|uat|deploy|observed_behavior (#3240)
```

The two sibling criteria (flowchart warning, payload-less event) completed with `kind: test` evidence.

## Expected

The required-axis classifier should tell these two kinds of criterion apart:
- one that requires a deployment to happen ("deployed to staging", "after deploy, …");
- one that describes how code handles deployment *data* (deploy.done frames, deployment status, rollbacks).

A noun phrase about deployment records should not need deploy evidence.

## Impact

- In a project that does not deploy until a release (here, nothing deploys before 5.0.0), any story whose code handles deployment events is blocked until an operator issues an `acceptance-disposition` grant.
- The only agent-side workaround is to reword the acceptance text, which edits the gate's input to go green (#3156).

## Suggested fix

Do one of these:
- Derive the deploy axis only from verbs or phrases that require a deployment event.
- Let `kind: test` satisfy a criterion whose subject is a deployment record, and say so in the error.
- Name the matched phrase in the error, so authors can see why the axis applied.

clauses.text: Explainer. A new exported `explainTextStrictAxes(item)` in `packages/core/src/scope/acceptance-evidence.ts` builds the same joined, lowercased, slash-split text that `inferTextStrictAxes` matches today, with an index map from each character back to its field and original index, and runs the same regexes over all matches. Per axis it returns up to 3 matches and a count of the rest. Each match gives the field holding its start, `crossField: true` when it ends in another field, and an excerpt: the matched words plus up to four words either side, sliced from the original field text through the map. `inferTextStrictAxes` takes its axis list from the explainer, so decision and explanation cannot drift.
Declared axes. When a declaration decides the axes, the report names the field that held the winning token and its value, using the existing precedence of the eight fields.
Fence. Every printed excerpt is cut to 80 characters first and then passed through `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText`.

Refusal detail. For an unsuitable `evidence.kind`, the `scope:complete` detail adds one continuation line per reported match (`<axis> from <field>: <excerpt>`, then `(+N more)`), or the declared field from item 2. When more than one strict axis is required, it says that no single evidence kind satisfies the clause.

Refusal remedy. When a blocker is an axis mismatch, the gate's closing text for that item replaces "Write evidence/disposition on the plan item at the reported path" with: record evidence of the required kind, or an operator runs `formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand` with `not_applicable`, the plan id when present and the item id. It states that the grant disposes of the whole criterion and replaces its evidence, that the grant is bound to the clause text (`clause.N` ids) or the item title only, and that #7127 tracks a correction that keeps test evidence. An item without an id is reported as not targetable by a grant. The refusal does not suggest rewording the clause or adding a declaration. `formatAcceptanceDispositionCommand` and its template-name constant move into `scope/acceptance-evidence.ts`; `policy/acceptance-disposition-grant.ts` re-exports them.

Advisories. At `scope:promote`, `scope:activate` and `xbrief:preflight` each row keeps its current text, and its reported matches print on indented continuation lines under it. At promote and activate the last line also says that a `merge` declaration means no strict axis, so test, review or merge evidence then passes. At `xbrief:preflight` the last line names the item 5 grant command and still does not suggest a declaration.
The classifier's results do not change, and existing axis expectations stay as they are.
